clue.text: What leading actors do to stop the old coach leaving

definitions.meaning: star performers command attention and keep the spotlight on themselves

definitions.text: to stop the old coach leaving
definitions.meaning: a stagecoach was the old horse-drawn coach, and to keep it from departing is to hold it

explanation.surface: A theatre note on star actors, oddly mixed with halting a coach.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the second half as HOLD THE STAGE(coach): 'stage' is short for stagecoach.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: star performers dominate the boards, and literally detaining a stagecoach is the second sense.

clue.text: The arms go out to a cheeky pet

indicators.note: the letters of the phrase are sent out of their order and rearranged

explanation.surface: Weapons are put away near a saucy pet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'go out' turns THE ARMS into the anagram that names the pet.
explanation.definitionFit: This rodent pet stores food in pouches in its cheeks, so it is literally cheeky.

clue.text: Watch, through the window apparently

definitions.meaning: a watch is a guard keeping vigil
gazing through a window is literally looking outside

explanation.surface: Someone keeps watch by peering through a window.
explanation.definitionFit: A sentry's post or vigil is one sense; the literal act of gazing outside is the other.

clue.text: Moscow's diocese, so it is said, opened to let the Jews through

definitions.text: opened to let the Jews through

indicators.note: signals that the phrase is spoken and the answer only matches its sound

parts.note: Moscow was the capital of the Reds (Soviet communists), and a see is a bishop's diocese

explanation.surface: A Russian church district somehow linked to the Exodus story.
explanation.walkthrough: 'so it is said' makes 'the Red see' sound like the sea that parted in Exodus.
explanation.definitionFit: In the Bible, Moses parted these waters so the Israelites could cross on dry land.

clue.text: Additional entry in the next race

indicators.note: the answer is found entered inside the run of letters that follows

explanation.surface: A late runner is added to the field for the coming race.
explanation.walkthrough: 'entry in' points into 'next race', where the letters run across the word join.
explanation.definitionFit: Something supplementary is over and above what is usual.

clue.text: A bit of rigging works in the end

indicators.note: one word is placed within the other in this clue

parts.note: the tail is the end of something
OPS, short for opuses, are works

explanation.surface: Part of a ship's ropes does its job at the last moment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts OPS inside TAIL.
explanation.definitionFit: This sail sits above the lowest sail on a mast, part of a ship's rig.

clue.text: A man from Tyneside gives little George a rough ride

parts.note: GEO is a short form of the name George

indicators.note: the word ride is roughed up so its letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A northerner bumps a small boy called George about.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rough' rearranges RIDE into RDIE. A Tyneside native is from the Newcastle area of north-east England.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the nickname for a native of Newcastle and Tyneside in north-east England.

clue.text: Prayer Book legislation which provides a service

definitions.text: Prayer Book legislation which provides a service

parts.words: Prayer Book legislation which provides a service
parts.note: reads as a parliamentary statute about church services; it is also simply a religious service

explanation.surface: A law about the Prayer Book sets out how church services run.
explanation.walkthrough: The phrase suggests a law (an Act), but the words also name a religious service itself.
explanation.definitionFit: A service of prayer and praise is devotion offered to God, and the phrase could also be read as a statute.

clue.text: Come around the saucepan for stewed fruit

indicators.note: the first word wraps itself around the second in this clue

parts.note: a pot is a saucepan

explanation.surface: An invitation to gather round the cooking pan for dessert.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' puts POT inside COME, split after COM.
explanation.definitionFit: This dessert is fruit cooked slowly in syrup.

clue.text: Bar advice on how to discover a secret door

definitions.meaning: a bar is a public drinking room in a pub

definitions.text: advice on how to discover a secret door
definitions.meaning: tapping a wall to find a hidden room is the second sense

explanation.surface: A pub, or a tip on finding a concealed doorway.
explanation.walkthrough: Split as TAP ROOM, the instruction to knock on walls to find a hollow chamber.
explanation.definitionFit: A pub bar where beer is drawn from the tap is one sense; knocking on walls to find a hidden chamber is the other.

clue.text: Fasts one term getting ready for a big beano

indicators.note: the letters are being prepared and rearranged into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone who fasted all term is preparing for a blowout.
explanation.walkthrough: 'getting ready' rearranges FASTS ONE TERM. A beano is British slang for a party or celebration.
explanation.definitionFit: A beano is a lively party or meal, and a huge banquet is a big one.

clue.text: Dismissed, swindled, and thoroughly beaten

parts.note: a batsman dismissed in cricket is out
done is slang for cheated

explanation.surface: A list of a cricketer's misfortunes: out, cheated and trounced.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a dismissed batsman is OUT; DONE is British slang for conned.
explanation.definitionFit: Surpassed or defeated decisively by a rival.

clue.text: A boy with a racket made his fortune with a lamp

definitions.text: made his fortune with a lamp
definitions.note: a verb phrase standing for the person who did this, the hero of the tale

parts.note: a lad is a boy
din is a racket or loud noise

explanation.surface: A noisy lad got rich thanks to a lamp.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition describes the pantomime hero whose magic lamp held a genie.
explanation.definitionFit: In the Arabian Nights tale, this hero gains riches from a genie in a magic lamp.

clue.text: Not the best way to beat your opponent

definitions.meaning: the opposite extreme from the finest
as a verb the word means to defeat

explanation.surface: A poor method of defeating a rival.
explanation.walkthrough: As a verb the answer means defeat, so the second sense is a way to beat someone.
explanation.definitionFit: The superlative of bad is one sense; to defeat or get the better of someone is the other.

clue.text: Unrecoverable money from even-odds in placing mad bets

indicators.note: one piece goes inside the other here
the bets are being placed, so their letters are set out in a new arrangement

parts.note: even odds are fifty-fifty, and fifty is L in Roman numerals, twice

explanation.surface: Money lost on even-money gambles by a reckless punter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'placing' rearranges MAD BETS into SMADEBT; 'in' puts LL (50-50) inside after SMA.
explanation.definitionFit: A minor sum owed that is not worth the cost of chasing is often written off.

clue.text: A sort of square drawing device to find the limit of a dynamic equation

definitions.text: the limit of a dynamic equation

parts.note: a T-square is a drawing instrument
a tractor draws, or pulls, loads

explanation.surface: A technical drawing tool for solving mathematical equations.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drawing' means pulling, not sketching: a tractor draws a plough.
explanation.definitionFit: In dynamical systems this is the set of states a system settles towards over time.

clue.text: Boisterous players may finish off the house

definitions.note: a noun sense: a coating finishing the outside of the house

parts.note: rough means rowdy
the cast are the actors in a production

explanation.surface: Rowdy actors might wreck the house.
explanation.walkthrough: 'finish off' suggests destroying the house, but here a finish is a wall coating.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a coarse render of plaster and gravel used to coat outside walls.

clue.text: Put opponent at a disadvantage, and away from the limelight

definitions.meaning: to outshine or divert attention from a rival
at the back of the stage, away from the audience

explanation.surface: Getting one over on a rival while staying out of view.
explanation.walkthrough: An actor who moves to the back of the stage forces others to turn away from the audience.
explanation.definitionFit: To outshine a rival is one sense; the rear of a theatre stage is the other.

clue.text: Offer, or wait for a better offer?

definitions.meaning: to hold something out is to extend or offer it
to refuse terms until better ones come

explanation.surface: A negotiator's question: make a bid, or wait?
explanation.definitionFit: Extend something towards someone is one sense; resist agreement until conditions improve is the other.

clue.text: Racehorse anxiously waiting for his stable mate to give birth?

definitions.meaning: a horse bred for harness racing at a lateral gait

definitions.text: anxiously waiting for his stable mate to give birth
definitions.meaning: an expectant father paces up and down waiting

explanation.surface: A stallion fretting while his mare foals.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stable mate' suggests horses, but also a steady partner; a nervous father-to-be paces the corridor.
explanation.definitionFit: A harness horse with a lateral gait is one sense; one who walks up and down nervously is the other.

clue.text: Forecast Alliance electoral policy proclamation

parts.note: the 1980s Liberal-SDP Alliance campaigned for proportional representation, PR
an edict is an official proclamation

explanation.surface: A statement of electoral policy from a centrist party.
explanation.walkthrough: The Alliance was the 1980s UK partnership of Liberals and Social Democrats, which campaigned for proportional representation.
explanation.definitionFit: To foretell what will happen; both are verbs.

clue.text: 150-love match leads to uproar

parts.note: CL is 150 in Roman numerals
an amour is a love affair

explanation.surface: A tennis score of 150-love leads to a riot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'love' and 'match' suggest tennis, but 'love match' is a romance.
explanation.definitionFit: A loud noisy outcry from a crowd.

clue.text: Wrangled despite being well equipped for polar travel

definitions.meaning: argued or harassed

definitions.text: being well equipped for polar travel
definitions.meaning: read as ..., owning a sledge for the ice

explanation.surface: A polar explorer quarrelled though properly kitted out.
explanation.walkthrough: Split as HAS SLED, someone who owns a sledge.
explanation.definitionFit: Bothered or argued with is one sense; owning a sledge is the other.

clue.text: What submissive types do if they want to postpone a decision

definitions.meaning: they yield to others' wishes
to put off until later

explanation.surface: Meek people delay making choices.
explanation.definitionFit: Yield to another's judgment is one sense; put off until later is the other.

clue.text: It is mean to declare what woman is loath to declare

parts.note: to aver is to declare

parts.words: what woman is loath to declare
parts.note: by old convention a woman keeps her age secret

explanation.surface: Unkind to reveal what a woman would rather not.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mean' looks like unkind but is the statistical sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Statistically, the arithmetic mean is a typical value.

clue.text: There will be no theatricals at the extra football match

definitions.meaning: read as ..., the show is cancelled
a deciding game after a tie or the regular season

explanation.surface: No more drama at the extra-time football game.
explanation.walkthrough: Split as PLAY OFF: the performance is cancelled.
explanation.definitionFit: A cancelled performance is one sense; a deciding match after a drawn contest is the other.

clue.text: Tradesmen who really do suit their customers

definitions.text: Tradesmen who really do suit their customers

parts.words: Tradesmen who really do suit their customers
parts.note: suit reads as please, but these craftsmen literally make suits for their clients

explanation.surface: Shopkeepers who satisfy their clients.
explanation.walkthrough: 'suit' means please, but these men cut and sew suits.
explanation.definitionFit: Garment makers who cut and sew clothes for clients make them suits.

clue.text: He corresponds to a child beginning his copybook

definitions.meaning: a person who sends correspondence
a child learning to form letters in a handwriting book

explanation.surface: A pen pal, or a child starting penmanship practice.
explanation.walkthrough: A copybook is a book of handwriting models a child copies to learn letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A correspondent is one sense; a child forming alphabet letters by hand is the other.
